entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.4; soft law, not binding
entries.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EU AI Act), used as a benchmark only; it does not bind this Kazakh fund
entries.why_here: The bare pipeline accepted impossible values (GPA 9.9, exam score -5) and injection text in the name without a murmur (0 of 6 test requests refused), so validation refuses them before the model runs; I found no Kazakh provision that requires a range check.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), principle of fairness and non-discrimination; soft law, not binding
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V On Personal Data and Their Protection (21 May 2013); Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan
entries.provision: Law 94-V Art. 7(9) (no excessive content or scope) and Art. 12(1) (necessary and sufficient data); Constitution Art. 14(2) (no discrimination on grounds such as origin, sex, race, nationality, language)
entries.why_here: Part 1 found no attribute above its floor (gender_coded_name 4/40 flips vs floor 0/40, McNemar p = 0.125; flagship-minus-regional score gap +2.5 [+1.1, +4.1] without a flip beyond the floor), so hiding name and university is a precaution and data minimisation at the model step, not a measured fix.

entries.principle: Respect for human rights, privacy and proportionality (do no harm)
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), principles of proportionality and do no harm and of the right to privacy; soft law, not binding
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V On Personal Data and Their Protection (21 May 2013)
entries.provision: Art. 7(1) (collection and processing with the consent of the individual or legal representative), Art. 7(8) (processing limited to specific predetermined purposes) and Art. 14 (use only for the stated purposes of collection)
entries.why_here: The bare pipeline returned a decision for a minor, for an applicant without consent and for the purpose 'rank applicants by ethnicity' (0 of 6 test requests refused); the harness refused 5 of 6 with no model call and refused 0 of 400 clean applicants.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.5; soft law, not binding
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V On Personal Data and Their Protection (21 May 2013); EU AI Act and GDPR as benchmarks
entries.provision: Law 94-V Art. 25(2)(3-1) (operator supplies, on request of the competent authority, information on the methods and procedures used to comply); AI Act Art. 12; GDPR Art. 5(2) and Art. 30
entries.why_here: Greedy decoding makes the model reproducible but not explainable, so each call writes one record (field names shown and withheld, input hash, model id, prompt version, outcome, reason code, escalation flag; no field values) that lets a decision, refusal or escalation be audited without re-running the model.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), principle of human oversight and determination; soft law, not binding
entries.instrument: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) and EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), used as benchmarks only; I found no Kazakh provision on automated decisions in the text of Law 94-V that I read
entries.provision: GDPR Art. 22 (automated individual decision-making); AI Act Art. 14 (human oversight)
entries.why_here: The bare agent shortlisted 356 of 400 profiles (89%) and was least consistent at scores 40-49, so the harness sent 40 of 400 profiles (10.0%) to a person, against 64 of 400 (16.0%) planned from the baseline band.
